chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Hello and welcome to this video lecture series on microprocessor and microcontroller.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And from this lecture onwards we are going to start this important concept of interfacing

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And we are going to study this interfacing in context of 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So first of all there are two things that we need to address before beginning this lecture.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Why are we studying interfacing in context of 8086 only?

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: We could have also studied this in context of 8085.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: But the thing there is that 8085 is fairly simple microprocessor as compared to 8086.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And 8086 has a separation of even and odd memory banks.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So some of the concepts of external memory interfacing are little more complicated as compared to

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So if you study them here it will be easy for you to study them for 8085 on your own.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's why we are using this 8086 microprocessor system.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: The second thing that we need to address here is that what are we going to do with this interfacing

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: thing?

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So the thing is microprocessor 8086 in itself is just like brain.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: It has got capability to do things but it won't be able to do things if we do not have peripherals

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: which are interfaced to itself.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So from microprocessor we need to create a micro control sorry a micro computer system.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: A micro computer system is a combination of a microprocessor together with its peripherals.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's what we are going to do.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: We have spent a fairly good time in studying 8086.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: It's fundamentals and now it is a time to create a micro computer system.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: A micro computer system will have this processor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: It will also have its peripherals like keyboard.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: It will have a monitor not the monitor that we see today but maybe a seven segment display

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: and various other things will be interfaced to it.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's what we are going to see.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So this is the 21st video lecture in the complete series and the first video lecture for interfacing.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And the topic of today's video is interfacing external memory 28086 as well as interfacing input

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: output devices or input output ports to 8086.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's what we are going to do.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: But before beginning this lecture let me just show you this syllabus that we have complete

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: up till now.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So you can see here we have completed 8085 first in great details.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: However, we didn't bring that this interfacing thing there because I saved it for 8086.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we have dedicated 10 lectures for 8086.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we started with architecture where we studied the hardware construction of 8083, the internal

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: hardware construction and what is the role of each and every element there.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Then we studied the pin diagram.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: I mean if you purchase the 8086 microprocessor, we will be able to access it through its pins.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we studied the detail of every pin and then we saw the programming model.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: In programming model, we saw what portions of microprocessor are accessible to us as programmers.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's what we saw there.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And we dedicated then the next three lectures for making simple programs in 8086.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So there we studied how to deal with the externally interfaced memory, how to do interrupts.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Interrupts we dedicated a separate lecture where we studied the interrupt structure and we made

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: some simple programs on how to deal with stack, how to deal with memory, how to do some simple

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: input outputs.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's what we covered there.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Then we studied the two modes, maximum mode and minimum mode of operation for 8086.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So it might be the case that 8086 is operating alone in the system.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's what we mean by minimum mode alone microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: If it is there, then it is minimum mode of operation.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And in maximum mode 8086 operates with other processors in the system, which might be another

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: 8086 or another math coprocessor or something else.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right. So that's what we studied in these two lectures.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Then after we started with addressing modes and instruction set part one, where we saw

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: the addressing modes primarily, how many addressing modes are there.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And then we started studying the instruction set.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we have dedicated one lecture to that, although we haven't been able to cover all the instructions

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: there because the list of instruction set of 8086 is fairly long as compared to 8085.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we will study them in the laboratory sessions because anyway, we are going to make programs

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: there. So instruction sets are best study by practicing them.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we are not going to dedicate any further lectures for studying instruction set.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: We will cover them when we will make programs in laboratory sessions.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So after that, we studied the memory organization of 8086 in the last lecture.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And that's what we need to remember for today's lecture also, because 8086 memory is different

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: from 8085 memory on various grounds.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: First of all, the memory is segmented.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So you can make four logical segments into your completely externally interfaced memory,

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: which is of one megabyte size.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Other than that, the hardware implementation of this memory is such that you need to have

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: an odd bank and an even bank.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right. And we studied that on the last lecture.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So let me just show you the slides and let us quickly revise that because that will be used in this lecture also.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we take a pilot.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: We took a pilot example where we said that if we had a memory which had only 16 locations and each location is of one byte.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So it could be either a single chip of 16 locations or it could be broken into two chips of eight locations each.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And that is called one of them as odd bank and other of other as even bank.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And since 8086 is a 16 bit microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So you have a data bus of 16 bits and that data bus.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: It's lower order by it is connected to this even bank and higher order by it is connected to this odd bank.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: But if you have only single memory chip, you cannot connect the entire data bus into the eight bits of one location.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Because ultimately out of this memory chip, you will have eight wires coming out or eight connections coming out to interface the data bus, which will be same for this.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: But then we have got a data bus of 16 bits.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So you need an additional hardware to interface this kind of memory to your system.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: However, here, since you have separated it in two parts, you can just put your complete data bus into these two chips at once.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And that is advantageous because if both of these memory banks are activated, which will happen when A0 is 0.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So this is active low signal.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So this will activate this even bank.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And if this BHE bar is also 0, so this is also active low signal.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: This will activate this particular bank.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So in one machine cycle only the complete data of 16 bits can be transferred to both of these chips.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that was the whole sole aim of dividing the memory into odd and even banks.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And odd and even banks are not named randomly.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Since if you see these yellow ones, if you see these yellow addresses, they all end in 0.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So whatever numbers end in 0, if you convert them to a decimal system, they will be all even.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So you can see that representation here.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: They are all even numbers.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: That is why A0 is used as a select line.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And regarding the address lines, if you see the address lines here, in this original chip, you had four address lines because you had 16 locations.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So 2 raised to the power of 4 is 16.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: However, in this, you can only have three address lines.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So what we have done is we have connected A1, A2 and A3.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: This A1, A2 and A3 here.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And you can see that A0 is used as a chip select signal for this particular even bank.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And for odd bank, we have got BHE bar.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we need to keep this in mind to be able to understand today's lecture.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So let me just come to today's lecture.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And in today's lecture, as we have already said that we are going to study the interfacing of memory and input output devices.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So let me just quickly begin by pointing out some important points about this interfacing thing.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So first of all, peripherals, they are of two types.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: I have written several points here.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: We will discuss these points one by one and we will see the relevant diagrams also.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So let's discuss these first two points first.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Peripherals are of two types.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: First is general purpose peripheral and second is dedicated peripherals.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: General purpose peripherals mean that you need to have a memory with a microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Because if you do not have memory, the microprocessor simply won't work.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Because the programs are written in the externally interfaced memory only.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: They are not written inside the internal registers of the microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So this is a general purpose peripheral.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: You need to have this.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Similarly, display is also essential.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: If you do not have a mechanism of seeing what's going on inside microprocessor in terms of obtaining your results, etc.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So you do not have very much use of that microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And similarly, you need to have a keyboard to interact, to be able to interact with that microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: We need to have keyboard.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And also you will need to have some input output ports.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Because if you have some USB device or in those days when these microprocessors were designed,

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: if you have some specialized chips which contain some data.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So you need to take data from those chips.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: For that you need to have some input output ports.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So these are general purpose peripherals.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: They need to be there.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: These are the basic minimum peripherals that should be there in the microprocessor so that it should be able to perform.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Then there are some dedicated peripherals.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Some dedicated peripherals are there.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Like this PIC, DMA and CRT controller.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Programmable interrupt controller, direct memory access and this cathode ray tube CRT controller.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So these dedicated peripherals are there.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: We will discuss more about them when we will study the interfacing of these things with this microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So there are two types of peripherals.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So now let's talk something about this semiconductor memory.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Semiconductor memory is of two types.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: RAM, which is again of two types.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Static RAM and Dynamic RAM.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Similarly, you have ROM.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: You are already aware of what RAM is.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Random Access Memory and ROM which is Read Only Memory.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So ROM usually contains some system critical programs which are used to run the system.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So ROM is there and you have RAM which is Random Access Memory.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And it is used to accelerate your programs.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: I mean, it is used to improve the speed in your computers as you know them now.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So RAM is of two types.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Static RAM and Dynamic RAM.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So static RAM is usually very costly and Dynamic RAM is less costly.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: It is actually very cheap.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So this static RAM actually acts as the cache memory of the system.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So Dynamic RAM is in actual sense the RAM that we put in our computers today.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So while if you want to improve the speed of system, you go to a shop and you buy some RAM

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: and put in the slot for the RAM on your motherboard.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's what we mean by a Dynamic RAM.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And static RAM usually is a cache memory which is usually present with the computer.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And it is actually very, very fast.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: There are some differences in construction of static and Dynamic RAM which makes them different,

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: which we are also going to discuss in this particular lecture.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: ROM similarly could be either static or Dynamic.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: But usually ROM is considered as static because we do not need ROM to be slow.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So that's why I haven't written static ROM and Dynamic ROM.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So if it is ROM, it is meant to be static only.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Then usually the memory is represented in this way.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: They will usually write this 4K cross 8.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: What will it mean?

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: It will simply mean that you have 4K location.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: 4K locations of 8 bit each.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Or an alternate way of writing this is you can simply write 4K bytes or 4Kb memory is required.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So 4K locations are there.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: You understand what Kilo is.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Kilo is 2 raised to the power of 10 in binary system, which is 1024.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So you will have 4 into 1024 locations and each location is of 1 byte.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So this is what we mean by representation of memory.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So whenever someone says I need to have a 4K cross 8 memory, they mean that they need to have a 4K byte of memory.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So another important point of interfacing the externally interface memory to your microprocessor is this.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: First of all, lower order address lines are used as address lines.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So if you are interfacing less memory, I mean the external interface memory, external interface memory can be of 1 megabytes.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: You do not usually use the complete 1 megabyte memory location for addresses.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: You have some less memory.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: You have purchased only few chips and you believe that your program will be able to run in that.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So why purchase a complete big chip?

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So on that end, if it is the case, then a good practice is that lower order address lines are used as address lines.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So we have got 20 address lines here because the address bus is of 20 bits.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And if you want to use full capacity of the address bus, then you will have complete 1 megabyte memory.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: But if you have any less memory, then it is preferred that you should begin from the starting addresses means 5 times 0, then 00001, 00002 and so on.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So it is preferred that you begin from the numerical order of memory only.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: You should interface your memory in that order.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Or if you interface it from some other location, it should be in continuous fashion.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: I mean, it should not be the case that you have one chip starting from 0000 and ending at suppose 64 kilobytes after that.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And after that, you leave some gap.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And then after you start your memory locations, although that is technically not impossible.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: That is done in some of the cases.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: But it is a good practice to keep your memory in continuous locations.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Then higher order address lines which are left.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: I mean, if you are using some less memory, then obviously less address lines will be used to address that complete memory.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So whatever lines are left, whatever address lines are left, those are higher order address lines and they are used for generation of chip select signals.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So this will become clear to us when we will see an example in this lecture only in a short while.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: At this point, I have already discussed.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: It is desired to use continuous locations for memory chip interfacing.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And I would also like to keep one more point here that when a microprocessor is reset, when a microprocessor is reset through external pin,

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: through external pin, then the control is transferred to FFFF0 in hexadecimal.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So when a microprocessor, when a microprocessor is reset through external pin, then the control is transferred to FFFF0H.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Mind you, I have written these five hexadecimal digits.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: I mean, the actual physical address here.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Right.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So this is also one of the important points to note that when a microprocessor is reset through external pin,

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: that is in the pin diagram of microprocessor, there is a reset pin.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: Then the control is transferred to FFFF0H.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: And whenever a microprocessor is reset, it will just start executing the programs which are written in its ROM.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: So it's a good practice to keep your ROM interfaced to this particular address.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
chunks.text: I mean, your ROM should include this address so that when a microprocessor is reset, it will start reading the instructions after that to be able to start the system.

chunks.title: Video 21 - Memory Interfacing
